intro: This branch introduces decimals, the numbers with a point like 2.75, which are another way to write tenths and hundredths. They connect fractions to money and measurement, and the learner learns to calculate with them.

II.7.01.what: Understanding tenths written as decimals, where 0.1 means one tenth of a whole.

levels.a: Sees that 0.1 is one tenth, so 0.2 is two tenths.
levels.b: Names the decimal shown by a bar cut into ten parts.
levels.c: Names decimals marked on a number line.
levels.d: Matches a decimal like 2.8 to its words, two and eight tenths.

II.7.02.what: Understanding hundredths written as decimals, where 0.01 means one hundredth of a whole.

levels.a: Writes a number of hundredths as a decimal, as in 81 hundredths is 0.81.
levels.b: Names the decimal shown on a grid of 100 squares.
levels.c: Matches a decimal like 1.83 to its words.
levels.d: Knows that 0.8 (eight tenths) is more than 0.06 (six hundredths).

II.7.03.what: Knowing what each digit after the decimal point is worth: tenths, then hundredths, then thousandths.

levels.a: Tells the value of a digit in the tenths place.
levels.b: Tells the value of a digit in the hundredths place.
levels.c: Tells the value of a digit in the thousandths place.
levels.d: Breaks a decimal into the value of each digit, as in 2.786 = 2 + 0.7 + 0.08 + 0.006.

II.7.04.what: Switching between fractions and decimals, since they are two ways of writing the same amount.

levels.a: Writes tenths as fractions and decimals, as in 0.8 is eight tenths.
levels.b: Writes hundredths as decimals, including fractions that can be scaled to hundredths.
levels.c: Knows the common ones: one half is 0.5, one quarter 0.25, three quarters 0.75.
levels.d: Writes a decimal as a fraction in simplest form.

II.7.05.what: Deciding which of two or more decimals is bigger, and putting them in order.

levels.a: Compares decimals with the same number of digits after the point.
levels.b: Compares decimals of different lengths, knowing 0.5 is more than 0.45.
levels.c: Names decimals on a finely marked number line.
levels.d: Puts a list of decimals in order from least to greatest.
levels.e: Counts which digits can fill a gap and keep a decimal comparison true.
levels.f: Counts every decimal with up to two places that lies between two given numbers.

II.7.06.what: Rounding decimals to a simpler nearby number, such as the nearest whole number or tenth.

levels.a: Rounds a decimal to the nearest whole number.
levels.b: Rounds a decimal to the nearest tenth.
levels.c: Rounds a decimal to the nearest hundredth.
levels.d: Rounds to estimate an answer, as in 9.8 times 6 is about 60.

II.7.07.what: Adding decimals, keeping the decimal points lined up so tenths add to tenths.

levels.b: Adds decimals with hundredths in columns.
levels.c: Lines up the points correctly when adding a whole number to a decimal.
levels.d: Adds decimals with different numbers of digits after the point.
levels.e: Finds missing digits in a decimal addition, using what was carried.
levels.f: Places four digits in two decimals to make a sum as close as possible to a target.

II.7.08.what: Subtracting decimals, keeping the decimal points lined up.

levels.b: Subtracts decimals with hundredths in columns, borrowing when needed.
levels.c: Lines up the points correctly when the numbers have different lengths.
levels.d: Subtracts a decimal from a whole number by filling in zeros, as in 17 minus 13.85.

II.7.09.what: Multiplying and dividing decimals by 10, 100 and 1,000, and understanding what really happens.

levels.b: Multiplies a decimal by 100 and by 1,000.
levels.d: Explains that the digits move to new places while the point stays still.

II.7.10.what: Multiplying a decimal by a whole number, like 8.3 times 8.

levels.a: Uses pictures of bars to multiply, such as 2 lots of 0.8.
levels.b: Uses the written method to multiply.
levels.c: Multiplies as if there were no point, then puts the point back in the right place.
levels.d: Estimates the answer by rounding first.

II.7.11.what: Multiplying one decimal by another, like 1.8 times 3.6.

levels.a: Uses a split rectangle (area model) to multiply the parts.
levels.b: Counts the digits after the points to place the point in the answer.
levels.c: Uses the written method to multiply decimals.
levels.d: Estimates the answer by rounding first.
levels.e: Works backwards: finds the missing number in a decimal multiplication.
levels.f: Uses one known product, like 15 times 23, to work out related decimal products quickly.

II.7.12.what: Dividing a decimal by a whole number, including money amounts.

levels.a: Shares a decimal amount on a hundred grid into equal groups.
levels.b: Uses long division, keeping the point in line.
levels.c: Adds zeros after the point to keep dividing until nothing is left.
levels.d: Shares a sum of money equally.

II.7.13.what: Dividing by a decimal, such as how many 0.8 m pieces fit in 16.8 m.

levels.a: Multiplies both numbers by 10 or 100 to make the divisor a whole number.
levels.b: Uses the written method to divide by a decimal.
levels.c: Estimates the answer by rounding first.
levels.d: Solves word problems, like cutting a ribbon into equal pieces.

II.7.14.what: Using decimals to work with money in dollars and cents.

levels.a: Writes cents as part of a dollar, as in 83 cents is $0.83.
levels.b: Adds and subtracts money, such as working out change.
levels.c: Multiplies a price by a number of items.
levels.d: Works out what is left of a budget after several purchases.
levels.e: Solves shopping problems that need several steps to find one item's price.
levels.f: Solves a puzzle: two items' total and difference in price are known; finds each price.
